people.gloss: Plain silk, the scroll before the painting
people.role: A founder (905) and head of Nhàn Vân Quán; paints the sky the pool holds, one cloud a day
people.appearance: A slight woman with ink in the creases of her fingers and a grey topknot pinned with a worn brush, who looks at the sky more often than at the person speaking to her.
people.backstory: Diệp Tố Quyên was born in 860 in Tang Ma Thành, a silk-weaver's daughter who wove the plain silk painters buy. At twenty she carried a bolt of her own silk across the strait to Đàm Ảnh Thành, where the mainland painters were painting the sky upside down in the pool (A152). One of them, the old Kha Đạm Mặc (kha_dam_mac), had found that ink ground with qi went on moving after the brush stopped. She became his disciple. In 905 Lạc Hà granted the two of them a dry steppe west of the city that no one wanted, and they founded the abbey there (V092, N-nhan_van-01). In 1010 Kha walked into the pool at dusk with his brush and was found drowned in the morning. She believes he went into the reflection, and she has led the abbey since. In 1062 the blind master Đoạn Thương Hải (doan_thuong_hai) settled at the pool (A155). Since then she paints for him what the water shows, and he tells her what he hears in it. She pays Lạc Hà's tribute in unsigned scrolls and lets its envoy Hách Ánh Hà (hach_anh_ha) set the price.
people.wants: To finish the painting Kha left half-done at the pool's edge, the sky of the morning in 705 when Cô Phàm's fleet sailed, and to see that no one after her tries to.
people.secret: In 1062 she painted the morning of 705 out of the pool for Đoạn, using the founder's art. In the reflected sky the fleet did not sink. Its sails went into a fog bank west of Tịch Chiếu Đảo that is on no chart and was not there the day before. She burned the painting and has told no one, because the founder died painting that sky and because she thinks the fog is still there.

people.role: Elder and keeper of the Pool House at Đàm Ảnh Thành; runs the abbey's scroll trade
people.appearance: A handsome, well-fed man in a grey silk robe of better cut than the abbey allows, with a jade weight on his scroll-case.
people.backstory: A ship-chandler's son from Triều Âm Thành, taken by the founder Kha Đạm Mặc (kha_dam_mac) as his last disciple in 990. Kha taught him the old reflection art and he has never once used it. He keeps the Pool House by the water at Đàm Ảnh Thành, teaches the painters there and sells the abbey's door scrolls in Triều Âm and Tương Phùng Thị (A148). He thinks Diệp Tố Quyên (diep_to_quyen) gives the abbey away, and Lạc Hà's Counting House agrees with him. In 1199 he showed the Counting House what the scrolls fetch, and Lạc Hà raised the tribute by a tenth. He resents paying it and has taken it out of the Pool House servants' rice.

people.role: The head's last true disciple; paints the blind master's days at the Pool House and hunts for the sail in the pool
people.appearance: A thin woman with her sleeves tied back and a smear of blue ink along one jaw, who paints standing up and never sits until she is told to.
people.backstory: Tần Đảo Ảnh was born in 1150 at the Pool House in Đàm Ảnh Thành. Her mother, the painter Tần Vãn Kính (tan_van_kinh), painted her own reflection-double to sit for her portraits, and in the winter of 1158 she could not take her face back from it (N-nhan_van-03). The head Diệp Tố Quyên (diep_to_quyen) raised the girl and made her a true disciple. Tần paints faster than anyone in the abbey and finishes almost nothing. At the Pool House she paints the blind master Đoạn Thương Hải's (doan_thuong_hai) days for him: she tells him what the pool shows, and he tells her what he hears in it. In 1199 he told her he had heard a sail in the pool. Since then she has worked at night on an art she has not been taught, the founder's way of painting an old sky back out of the water. The island warden Lận Viễn Phàm (lan_vien_pham) has offered to pay for any sail she finds.
people.wants: To paint the sail Đoạn heard out of the pool, and to learn where her mother's face went.
people.secret: She has painted a reflection-double of herself, as her mother did, to sit in her place at the morning lesson while she sleeps off her nights at the pool. The double is getting better at sitting still than she is. Last month Mễ Phù Vân corrected its brushwork for an hour and did not notice.

people.role: Steward of the abbey's paper mill at Lục Trúc Thôn and the canes of Vạn Can Lâm
people.appearance: A broad, stooped man with pulp to the elbows and a straw hat he wears indoors.
people.backstory: A cane-cutter's son from Phù Can Thôn who has kept the abbey's paper mill at Lục Trúc Thôn for sixty years and cuts its canes in Vạn Can Lâm. Every sheet the abbey paints on has passed through his hands. He was Diệp Tố Quyên's (diep_to_quyen) disciple for forty years and knows he paints badly. Lạc Hà assesses the abbey's tribute in sheets, and for sixty years he argued the count with its collector Cận Thủ Chuyết (can_thu_chuyet) every autumn. Since the raise of 1199 the count runs all year at the Pool House, so he sends down a double he painted himself, rolled in the sheet cart. He paints badly, and it can only nod.

He signs a few of them, which the abbey forbids, because a signed scroll sells for three times as much. Lạc Hà's Tăng Vân Tiêu (tang_van_tieu) buys the signed ones for his stalls on the mainland and knows exactly what they are. people.backstory: A scholar's son from Phong Lâm Trấn on the mainland who came to Đàm Ảnh Thành in 800 to paint the sky upside down in the pool (A152). He found that ink ground with qi went on moving after the brush stopped. With his disciple Diệp Tố Quyên (diep_to_quyen) he founded the abbey in 905 (V092). In his last years he painted only old reflections, skies the pool had held before he was born. He died in 1010 with half the sky of 705 on his silk (N-nhan_van-02).
